sections.h2: What is Okaloosa County like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Okaloosa County is the most populous of the four counties in this set, with 221,810 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, up 4.8 percent since April 2020. It covers 930.19 square miles of land.

The 2020 to 2024 figures give a feel for the housing stock. Median owner-occupied value is $351,200, the owner-occupied rate is 68.4 percent, and median gross rent is $1,612. There are 108,608 housing units and 85,411 households. About 18.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 31,494 are veterans, which makes the military and age exemptions below a frequent topic for sellers.

  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,057.
  • Mean commute: 26.3 minutes.
  • Median household income: $81,998 (2024 dollars).

sections.h2: When do Okaloosa County tax bills go out and when are they due?
sections.html:
The tax collector begins collecting on November 1 for the January through December tax year. Statements are mailed on or before that date, and the gross amount is due by March 31.

  • 4 percent discount for November payment.
  • 3 percent in December.
  • 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.
  • No discount in March, and taxes are delinquent April 1.

The collector's calendar adds that a 3 percent penalty hits real property taxes in April and reminder notices of unpaid taxes are mailed by April 10. Mail payments by check, cashier's check or money order. In person, cash and cards also work, and card payments carry a bank card user fee. Delinquent amounts must be paid in cash, cashier's check or money order, and the amount due depends on the date the office receives the payment.

sections.h2: How does the Okaloosa County installment plan work?
sections.html:
The county offers a four-payment plan for owners whose estimated taxes exceed $100 and who do not pay through escrow. The application is due before May 1 and can be filed in the office or online.

Okaloosa installment plan schedule (source: okaloosatax.com real estate taxes page)
InstallmentDueShare and discount printed
FirstJuly 31One quarter of estimated taxes, 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30
SecondSeptember 30One quarter, 4.5 percent discount
ThirdDecember 31One quarter plus half of any adjustment, 3 percent discount
FourthMarch 31One quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, no discount

Missing the first payment cancels the plan, and the full amount is due by March 31 of the following year. Participants are re-enrolled automatically, and discounts do not apply to delinquent payments. If you sell mid-plan, tell the title company so the balance is settled at closing.

sections.h2: What exemptions matter in Okaloosa County?
sections.html:
With about a tenth of the population a veteran, the military-related reductions deserve attention. The state lists a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember with 10 percent or more disability, a homestead discount for veterans 65 and older with a permanent service-connected disability, and a possible total exemption for total and permanent disability.

A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing the exemption, a rule that can help owners on orders away from the county. Deployed servicemembers can claim a share of the exemption on Form DR-501M.

The standard homestead exemption is up to $50,000, filed on Form DR-501 with the property appraiser by March 1. Address updates also go through the property appraiser, who can be reached at (850) 651-7240 per the tax collector's page. Ask the appraiser's office whether the optional senior exemption for owners 65 and up is in force and what income limit applies.

sections.h2: What happens if Okaloosa County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The collector must advertise delinquent parcels once a week for three consecutive weeks, and advertising and collection fees are added to the bill. A tax certificate sale begins on or before June 1 on LienHub, bidding down from 18 percent, and the lowest bid takes the certificate.

A certificate lasts seven years and becomes an enforceable first lien. To remove it, the owner pays the delinquent tax, interest, penalties and advertising fees. After two or more years from delinquency the holder can apply for a tax deed, and the sale is run by the clerk of court. The collector also sells county-held certificates that earn 18 percent.

State statute adds that the opening bid on homestead land includes half of the assessed value, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit with the balance due within 24 hours. A seller with any unpaid year should clear it before listing.

sections.h2: How should an Okaloosa County seller handle taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Ask the title company to prorate the current year and to confirm no earlier year is open. The year of sale is billed in the following November, so the settlement statement uses an estimate.

Documentary stamp tax on the deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. The revenue department says taxable deeds include warranty, special warranty, quit claim and certificate of title, with an exemption for certain spousal and divorce transfers of homestead. The clerk collects the tax at recording, along with page charges of $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page under section 28.24.

Remember that Save Our Homes ends at sale. The state's chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026, so a long-time owner may hold a gap between assessed and just value that the buyer will not receive.

faqs.q: What does an Okaloosa County owner pay if taxes are late?
faqs.a: A 3 percent penalty is added to real property taxes in April, per the collector's calendar. Fees for advertising and collection are added too, and the delinquent amount depends on the receipt date.

faqs.q: How do I join the Okaloosa County installment plan?
faqs.a: File the application with the tax collector before May 1, in the office or online. Your estimated taxes must exceed $100 and cannot be paid through escrow.

faqs.q: When is the first Okaloosa installment due?
faqs.a: July 31, with a 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30. Missing it cancels the plan and the full bill is due the next March 31.

faqs.q: Who changes my mailing address for Okaloosa tax bills?
faqs.a: The property appraiser. The tax collector's page says address changes are processed there and gives (850) 651-7240 and www.okaloosapa.com.

faqs.q: Who conducts Okaloosa tax deed sales?
faqs.a: The clerk of court holds the public auction after a deed application. The tax collector handles the earlier certificate sale online.
